answer: A sybil tax blocks bulk fake identities. Each new identity pays a one-time, non-refundable tax of 40 credits, burned on payment, before it can list juniper seedlings. One payment unlocks only one identity, so a timber merchant cannot reuse one tax across many storefronts. Creating 1,000 fakes costs 40,000 credits up front, far above the profit from flooding a market, while an honest saffron seller pays 40 once and earns undiluted rewards.
